title: Termu-inator reachable acceptance contract
rationale: Completion was previously defined as a canonical + benchmark run on a physical Samsung S22U device in Termux, sealed to a commit/wheel identity. That gate is unreachable from any host without the device, so the 'canonical' verdict stayed permanently FAIL/not-run while 600+ local tests always passed. This contract replaces the unreachable gate with criteria that a developer machine or CI runner can actually execute and pass, terminating a candidate without a device. The physical-device benchmark is retained ONLY as an optional, informational signal that never blocks completion.

blocking_criteria.description: The full in-repo test suite passes with zero failures and zero errors.
blocking_criteria.replaces: Local-correctness portion of the old canonical run.

blocking_criteria.description: The full observe->act->verify loop runs end-to-end against a REAL headless browser (Chrome/Chromium/Firefox) driving the deterministic in-repo FixtureSite, using the production ObservationEngine, ActionRiskClassifier, element bindings, and CDP client. This exercises real DOM semantics, real form-effect counting, stale node-identity replacement, unavailable/hidden targets, challenge (login/OTP) takeover detection, prompt-injection inertness, and lost-response replay safety.
blocking_criteria.replaces: The unreachable S22U end-to-end device benchmark. This is the reachable equivalent: a real browser, real engine code, deterministic site.

blocking_criteria.description: The verdict is bound to a concrete repository identity (git commit SHA + working-tree hash). A candidate is identified by its resolved tree, not by a promise to commit later.
blocking_criteria.replaces: The 'obtain the user's new clean commit SHA before sealing' ritual, which never terminated because sealing waited on the device run.

informational_criteria.description: Optional Samsung S22U / Termux canonical + benchmark run. Provides field-hardware signal but is NOT required for completion. Its absence records as 'not_run', never as FAIL, and never blocks the verdict.
